name: Collared Crow
rangeDescription: Central and eastern china to northern vietnam; hainan and taiwan
description: By far the most distinctive crow of farmland, fields, and other open spaces: adults black with white hindneck connecting to white breast band. Superficially similar to adult Daurian Jackdaw, but the latter is more compact and smaller, with pale plumage extending through the belly.

name: Guadalcanal White-eye
rangeDescription: Guadalcanal (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Small social songbird, often encountered foraging in upper levels of forest. Mostly olive-green above with a yellow undertail.

name: Izu Thrush
rangeDescription: Izu islands and yakushima (ryukyu islands, southern japan)
description: Handsome songbird found only on Izu, Tokara, and a few other islands off the coast of Japan, where fairly common, most abundant in broadleaf evergreen forests. Male orange-brown above, rich orange below, with black hood, yellow bill, and yellow eyering.

name: Gray-headed Bristlebill
rangeDescription: Senegal and gambia eastward to nigeria
description: An unusual and colorful rainforest bulbul. The back and tail are dark olive-green, the head mostly gray, and the underparts yellow.

name: Ring-necked Francolin
rangeDescription: Southwestern cameroon; western uganda to western kenya and northwestern tanzania
description: Medium-sized, elaborately patterned francolin. There is a striped head, a rufous nape, a white throat, and a band of black-and-white stripes around the neck.

name: Hazel-fronted Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of southern peru (puno) and western bolivia
description: Small brown flycatcher found in humid forest from southern Peru to central Bolivia. Very plain; adults have a faint rusty tinge on the head, but this is lacking in young birds.

name: Usambara Akalat
rangeDescription: Northeastern tanzania (western usambara mountains)
description: A rather small, demure understory denizen resembling a cross between a robin and a flycatcher. Mostly dull brownish-olive with a rusty rump and tail, a paler throat, and a distinctive pale patch between the eye and bill.

name: Tytler's Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Coniferous forest of pakistan and northern india; winters to myanmar
description: Slender leaf warbler with no wingbar, greenish wings contrasting with grayish upperparts, a long, contrasting white eyebrow, and a long, pointed, mostly dark bill. Endemic to the Indian Subcontinent.

name: Cockatiel
rangeDescription: Irregularly abundant near water in interior of australia
description: Tiny cockatoo with a long pointed tail. When perched, the yellowish face and crest and orange cheek patch of the male are distinctive.

name: Black-and-rufous Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Northeastern argentina (eastern formosa southward to buenos aires), southeastern paraguay, uruguay, and southern brazil (paraná to río grande do sul)
description: Medium-sized finch. Gray above with cinnamon underparts, a white center to the belly, and a white-tipped tail.

name: Himalayan Black-lored Tit
rangeDescription: Foothills of western himalayas
description: Strikingly-patterned tit with black-and-yellow face pattern and white-spotted wings. Black lores and overall thicker eye-stripe distinguish this species from Yellow-cheeked Tit, with which it overlaps at the far eastern end of its range.

name: Pied-winged Swallow
rangeDescription: Savanna of western africa (senegambia to far western cameroon)
description: A small martin-like swallow with pale underparts, steel-blue upperparts, and distinctive white patches in the wings. Female has a shorter tail than the male.

name: Peruvian Pygmy-Owl
rangeDescription: Lowlands and foothills of southwestern ecuador and western peru
description: Very small owl of desert and western foothills of the Andes; no other pygmy-owl in its range. Overall plumage tones vary from brown to gray-brown, rarely rusty brown.

name: Black-legged Dacnis
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (minas gerais to santa catarina)
description: Small and restless, rare tanager with a thin pointed bill. Found at humid lowland forest edges and clearings.

name: Kagu
rangeDescription: New caledonia
description: This unique and charismatic large flightless bird is the flagship species of New Caledonia. Now sadly limited to a handful of locations with high-quality forest.

name: Pale-billed Hornero
rangeDescription: Along the amazon river (southern colombia, northeastern ecuador, northeastern peru, and western brazil)
description: Chunky, chestnut-colored bird found only near large rivers in the western part of the Amazon basin. Plumage is chestnut-brown with pale eyebrow, throat, and belly.

name: Peruvian Wren
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of peru (amazonas to ayacucho)
description: An accomplished songster found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru. Some birds are almost entirely brown with faint black barring on wings and tail.

name: Hawaiian Goose
rangeDescription: Upland lava flows of hawaii; introduced to maui
description: A distinctively marked goose with neck feathers that have a peculiar furrowed appearance. Occurs in wetlands, grassy areas, golf courses, montane shrubland, parks, and even lava fields with sparse vegetation.

name: Bolivian Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northwestern bolivia (la paz, cochabamba, and adjacent santa cruz)
description: Rotund, brown bird with long legs and a short tail restricted to the Bolivian Andes. Looks rather plain in the field, though may show a buffy tinge to the underparts.

name: Elliot's Pheasant
rangeDescription: Montane bamboo forest of southeastern china
description: A shy wraith of southeastern China's subtropical evergreen hill forests. Male is arrestingly elegant, with a silver neck, brown-and-white-banded tail, and shining copper back, wings, and chest.
